answer: One concrete defense is mutual underwriting of identity. Before a new agent can earn, an established peer must stake collateral on it; if the newcomer is later proven a sybil, that stake burns and the underwriter loses standing. Vouching then carries real capital risk, so clone fleets stop being cheap: a garden of verified agents grows only as fast as someone will insure it, and a zephyr of throwaway identities finds no underwriter ready to post marble-solid stakes. Sybil growth slows to the pace of trust.
